title: A Generated File's Metadata Must Not Change Unless Its Real Content Does — Otherwise Every Independent Rebuild Is a Manufactured Merge Conflict
problem: PR #50 hit a real GitHub merge conflict in data/status.json: the branch had regenerated the file after PR #49 merged, main's own auto-rebuild commit (.github/workflows/build-index.yml) had also regenerated it independently in the meantime, and the two copies conflicted — not because the underlying tech-debt/enhancement/open-discussion content actually differed, but because lib/build-status.js stamped _meta.generated (a wall-clock ISO timestamp) and _meta.commit (the git SHA at build time) into the file on every single run. Two builds of identical source data produced two different files purely because of when and on what commit each one happened to run.
exploration: the existing lesson (generated-file-merge-driver-needs-local-registration.json) already named that .gitattributes' merge=ours can't be relied on in this environment — but that lesson addresses how to resolve a conflict once it exists, not why one was manufactured in the first place

checked whether GitHub's own web-based conflict UI would even honor a registered merge=ours driver if one existed — it doesn't; GitHub's server-side merge machinery doesn't consult .gitattributes custom drivers at all, so a driver-registration fix wouldn't have helped here regardless of the container/session issue

checked whether _meta.generated/_meta.commit were consumed anywhere (pages/ecosystem-hub.html, any test beyond a bare existence check) — neither was; they were pure unused byproduct, not information anyone actually needed

initially treated data/index.json builtAt and sw.js's commit-based cache key as justified because they were consumed; PR #141's exact-head generation review later proved that consumption alone does not require volatility and that both values prevented the reviewed commit from reproducing its own tree

replayed workflow steps after committing the first repair and found upstream clocks in data/index.json and identity-index.json plus sitemap git-history coupling; the content-derived service-worker fingerprint correctly exposed those inputs instead of hiding them
decision: Removed unused clock/commit metadata from status and identity projections; replaced index builtAt and the service-worker HEAD key with content fingerprints; removed clock displays from generated pages; omitted sitemap lastmod where the only available date was artifact history; and changed Build CI from a branch-writing correction bot into a read-only regenerate-and-diff gate. A genuine content difference still changes the output and remains reviewable.
lesson: Before stamping a wall clock, commit SHA, or generated-file git date into a committed build artifact, ask whether the value's meaning specifically requires that volatility. Being displayed or technically consumed is not enough. The default contract is same authored inputs → byte-identical output; content identity should be content-derived, and unavailable freshness should be omitted rather than inferred from the build container or carrying commit.
impact: Closed the original data/status.json conflict class and the later PR #141 exact-head closure failure across data/index.json, identity-index.json, sitemap.xml, generated page clocks, sw.js, and the artifact workflow. CI can now verify one immutable review head without pushing a bot correction or requiring a second account/fork to iterate around GH013.
